[資訊管理導論] Question 2

Apple has officially announced a multi-year partnership to integrate Google's Gemini AI model into its Siri voice assistant. According to a joint statement, Apple concluded that Google's technology offers the most robust foundation for its "Apple Foundation Models," enabling a new generation of generative AI experiences for users. The partnership is intended to accelerate Apple's AI roadmap, which encountered setbacks and delays following its initial teaser at the 2024 Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC). Analysts note that while reliance on an external partner underscores Apple's difficulties in developing a competitive in-house model, the agreement represents a strategic necessity. By leveraging Google's cloud computing and AI infrastructure, Apple aims to alleviate investor concerns about its perceived lag in the AI arms race and to stimulate iPhone demand through enhanced device capabilities.

Based on the case study, please address the following questions:

(A). Apple's traditional sources of competitive advantage reside in ecosystem lock-in and superior user experience. Analyze how Apple's decision to adopt an external AI model (Google Gemini), rather than relying exclusively on in-house development, may help preserve or even strengthen its competitive position in the mobile device market. (10%)

(B). Google functions simultaneously as a critical technology partner within Apple's iOS ecosystem and as the leader of the rival Android platform. Discuss the strategic risks (e.g., technological dependency) and potential benefits (e.g., reduced development time) associated with this co-opetitive relationship. (10%)

(C). Apple has historically positioned user privacy as a core source of sustained competitive advantage. Given Google's data-driven business model, analyze how Apple should design its product architecture and/or communication strategy to ensure that its competitive advantage based on user trust is not undermined by this partnership. (10%)
